body.text: The Polysemantic Superposition Problem in Deep Networks

Most coverage of Sparse Autoencoders in Foundation Models misses the structural details that actually matter in technology. When you look closely at real-world evidence, clear patterns emerge that separate durable results from short-term noise.

Standard transformer architectures compress vastly more real-world concepts into their hidden representations than they possess geometric dimensions. This phenomenon, known as superposition, forces individual residual stream neurons to act polysemantically: firing for quantum physics, culinary herbs, and legal clauses simultaneously. To decode the internal representations of frontier artificial intelligence, mechanistic interpretability researchers are training overcomplete sparse autoencoders (SAEs) which unpack these tangled activations into isolated, monosemantic features.

body.text: Training Overcomplete Sparse Dictionaries with TopK Activations

Recent breakthroughs replace traditional L1 regularization penalties with TopK activation functions. In TopK SAEs, only the K highest-magnitude latents are permitted to activate per forward pass, eliminating shrinkage bias and drastically improving reconstruction fidelity while preserving extreme concept sparsity across hundred-million-parameter dictionaries.
